correctness.rationale: All 27 ternary substitutions into the set {0,x,y} reduce to zero/equality, 2x=0, 2y=0, 2x=y, 2y=x, and x+y=0. For p>=7 each nonzero anchor sees distinct special targets 0,x,2x,x/2,-x and at least one generic target. Matching these profiles after either pebble is moved preserves the entire atomic diagram indefinitely, proving unrestricted-depth FO2 equivalence. Explicit FO1/FO2 sentences single out 2,3,5 and generic >=7. The D_n recursion defines n*x using only x,y,z by alternation and yields an FO3 torsion sentence singling out each prime. The standalone checker passed 91 cross-prime profile comparisons and 49 recursively constructed formula evaluations; these finite calculations are not the proof of the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The prime-order family is an algebraically canonical infinite class in an established finite-model-theory signature. The sharp FO1/FO2/FO3 transition is a complete natural classification, not a parameter-chosen finite sample: all characteristics >=7 collapse at width two but every characteristic becomes recognizable with three names. The permanent pebble-game mechanism explains the cutoff and answers, for prime cyclic groups only, the finite-variable bound question highlighted in Gomaa (2007) §3.9. The result does not claim a general theorem for all finite abelian groups.
